role: Interstate planning body, NIPC/Northwestern Indiana Regional Planning Commission
stance_basis: narrator paraphrase states Interstate Planning Committee concurred with NIPC's position finding project consistent with regional planning
summary: The Interstate Planning Committee reviewed the Lincoln Highway improvement project after it was judged to be of interstate significance under joint NIPC/Northwestern Indiana Regional Planning Commission procedures. At a meeting on May 22, 1974, the Committee concurred with NIPC's finding that the project was consistent with regional planning policies, effectively endorsing the project.
complaint_summary: The Interstate Planning Committee, at its May 22, 1974 meeting, concurred with the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission's position that the Lincoln Highway improvement project is consistent with regional planning policies.
summary_quote: The Committee was satisfied that there was no unresolved conflict between the two jurisdictions, N.E. Illinois and N.W. Indiana, and voted unanimously to endorse the application without additional comments.

mentions.quote: At a meeting held May 22, 1974 the Interstate Planning Committee concurred with the position taken by the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission.

The Committee was satisfied that there was no unresolved conflict between the two jurisdictions, N.E. Illinois and N.W. Indiana, and voted unanimously to endorse the application without additional comments.
